I have more than twelve years' experience in analytics in regulated banking and financial services. I
came into the industry straight from school and built my academic grounding alongside work, most recently
through an MSc in Financial Services.

The question that draws me to research is not whether a model looks good on a backtest, but whether it
holds up on data it has never seen, and whether a result is real or an artefact of how many things were
tried. That shapes how I work: state the hypothesis first, compare against a fair benchmark, and report
results whether or not they support the idea.

## Experience

- **Leading advanced analytics and business intelligence** in a bank, covering predictive analytics,
  machine learning and AI-enabled decision support, and leading analysts and data scientists.
- **Designing semantic layers, data dictionaries and lineage** so that analytical and AI outputs are
  consistent, traceable and explainable. This is the same discipline behind the semantic layer in my
  [proposed architecture](phd/index.qmd).
- **Leading data delivery for credit-risk impairment models** (probability of default, loss given default
  and exposure at default under IFRS 9), from source data and feature design through quality assurance,
  testing and production, with the documentation needed for audit and regulatory review.
- **Earlier roles** in regulatory and customer-remediation programmes, and in predictive analytics and data
  modelling for insurance and corporate clients.

## Where I need to grow

The proposal sits where quantitative finance meets AI. I am deliberately strengthening the parts my
background covers least: financial econometrics, forecast evaluation, and the established asset-pricing
and forecasting literature, which I am working through from AJG-ranked journals. The
[core reading](phd/index.qmd#core-reading) is listed with the proposal.

## How this site was built

I use AI tools in building this site, for writing code, generating figures and drafting prose, working
from my own research questions, design choices and interpretation. The judgement about what to test, what
it means and what to conclude is mine. I use these tools deliberately and say so openly; they help me
build faster, but they do not replace the understanding this site is meant to demonstrate.
